picks.style: vedic hymn, tanpura drone, deep male voice, slow, reverent, sparse
picks.why: The hymn to the Waters — within them immortality, within them medicine — with a mother-and-milk refrain.

picks.style: monsoon invocation, low drone, mridangam and rain-stick, layered male voices, building, elated
picks.why: The rain hymn ending with the frogs who kept silence a year like vow-keeping Brahmins and then spoke.

picks.style: sunrise chant, tanpura and bansuri, bright male voice, rising, radiant, unhurried
picks.why: The stars slipping away like thieves before the all-seeing Sun, drawn by seven tawny mares.

picks.style: roman comic patter, tibia and clappers, snarling old man's voice, fast, cantankerous
picks.why: The miser's opening tirade driving the old slave out of the house — pure kinetic comedy.

picks.style: comic monologue song, tibia and hand drum, agitated male voice, jittery, quickening
picks.why: Euclio and the cock that scratched too near the buried pot, and lost its head for it.

picks.style: slave's protest song, low strings and drum, sardonic male voice, steady, mounting
picks.why: Masters called Harpies and Tantali, poor amid wealth, thirsty in the middle of the ocean.

picks.style: trickster's aria, tibia and plucked strings, sly male voice, brisk, gleeful
picks.why: No soil in Attica so fertile as this old man — silver summoned out of a locked and sealed chest.

picks.style: comic soliloquy, low tibia and drum, anxious male voice, urgent, restless
picks.why: The slave alone, with mountains of misfortune about to tumble on him and no plan that pleases.

picks.style: reflective roman song, lyre and soft flute, older male voice, measured, rueful
picks.why: The wish for a mirror that shows the heart rather than the face, and one's own youth reflected back.

picks.style: roman lyric, lyre and soft aulos, warm baritone, unhurried, wine-lit
picks.why: Ask not what the morning brings; count each day as gain — carpe diem in its home register.

picks.style: sympotic song, kithara and low drum, relaxed male voice, easy, sunlit, ambling
picks.why: Grey heads under the plane tree, roses and Syrian scent, drinking while we may.

picks.style: bacchic ode, frame drum, pipes and shivering strings, ecstatic male voice, wild, accelerating
picks.why: No one leaps the tomb — then the sudden vision of Bacchus teaching Dryads, and the cry Evoe.

picks.style: english hymn, chamber organ and small choir, steady, plain, resolute
picks.why: Though fig and vine and fold all fail — yet still to Thee; a complete hymn of defiant trust.

picks.style: autumn air, acoustic guitar and viola, warm alto, slow, wistful
picks.why: Swallows leaving, flowers on their stems declining, and the line that life's a flower, a day a span.

picks.style: exile lament, solo harp and low male voice, mournful, spare, deliberate
picks.why: How shall the captive people sing in a strange clime — the psalm of the hung-up harps in full voice.

picks.style: revolutionary declamation, martial drum and brass, forceful male voice, driving, anthemic
picks.why: The sword lifted for freedom as the Word made flesh — a marching catalogue that builds line by line.

picks.style: verse-drama monologue, low strings and timpani, grave male voice, deliberate, swelling
picks.why: Wear the colour of your own flag; show not the end but the way — counsel written to be spoken aloud.

picks.style: visionary folk ballad, bodhran and bouzouki, low male voice, hypnotic, strange, mid-tempo
picks.why: Rivers running with red beer and brown, and the black-robed rider singing his song of deicides.

picks.style: pastoral lament, single lute, aging male voice, quiet, faltering, slow
picks.why: Time bears all things away, the mind as well — and now the songs are gone and the voice fails.
